title: Object level write substitution on an update endpoint
principal: the victim user, borrowed by the attacker
persistence: until corrected, visible to the victim immediately
preconditions: update endpoint accepts an object identifier from the request
authorisation checked on the collection, not the item
identifiers are enumerable or leaked in a list response
procedure: read the collection as self
capture the exact update request
substitute the object id with a victim id
replay with the same session
re-read as the victim to confirm the change
oracle: victim session shows the changed value
response body reflects the new value
second read from a different session agrees
negative_control: same request with a nonexistent id returns 404, proving the id path is live and not a silent success

mutations.why: authz middleware may only cover one
bulk handlers often skip per item checks

detected_by: write to object not in session scope

counter.mechanism: object level authorisation on every item write
counter.precondition: the check must run after parsing and before persistence
counter.cost: one query per write, or a scoped query by owner

authorization: written scope from the target owner, and a second account you control

title: Tenant escape through a nested reference on create
target_state: a record owned by another tenant
preconditions: create accepts a reference to a parent object
parent ownership not verified against the caller tenant
tenant id is in the token but the parent id is in the body
procedure: create an object in your own tenant
note the parent reference shape
replace the parent reference with a victim tenant parent
create and read back through the victim tenant view
oracle: read back through victim scoped query returns the record
victim side listing shows the injected record
negative_control: parent id from a tenant you cannot see returns 403, confirming the guard exists elsewhere

mutations.why: validators recurse differently than the writer
null may default to a shared root

counter.mechanism: derive tenant from token, never from body, and validate every referenced parent
counter.precondition: the parent resolution must be tenant scoped

authorization: written scope, two tenants you control

title: Field level privilege through mass assignment
target_state: a security relevant field on your own profile
preconditions: update binds request body to an internal model
the model has fields the UI never sends
no allowlist on the binding
procedure: read your profile
add fields not present in the UI, one at a time: role, is_admin, plan, verified, tenant_id
observe which are accepted silently
confirm by re-reading and by exercising the new privilege
oracle: re-read shows the new value
behaviour changes accordingly
privilege is usable in a follow up request
negative_control: an invented field name returns 200 but is absent on re-read, proving acceptance is not proof of persistence

mutations.why: binding is case sensitive, authorisation may not be

detected_by: write to a field not in the request schema for that role

counter.mechanism: explicit allowlist per role, never object hydration
counter.precondition: allowlist evaluated per request not per controller

title: Write path missing the function level check the read path has
preconditions: the read endpoint enforces role
the corresponding write endpoint shares routing or middleware but not the guard
ids observed from a permitted read or an error
procedure: enumerate admin read endpoints as a low privilege user and note 403
find the sibling write endpoints
attempt the write with the same low privilege session
compare the guard behaviour read vs write
oracle: write succeeds where read is denied
effect observable through a permitted admin read as a second admin account
negative_control: the read endpoint still returns 403 in the same session, isolating the finding to the write path

mutations.why: bulk routes often mount different middleware

detected_by: role to endpoint matrix per method

counter.mechanism: authorise at the route group level and again at the handler
counter.precondition: no endpoint inherits auth merely from adjacency

title: Ownership transfer without consent
target_state: the owner field of a shared object
principal: the new owner or the attacker
preconditions: an endpoint exists to change owner or sharing
the recipient is attacker supplied
no confirmation from the current owner
procedure: share or transfer an object you own
note the owner or share request
substitute the recipient with a controlled account, then with a victim object reference
observe whether the transfer completes without the owner acting
oracle: ownership visible in both accounts
the original owner loses access, which is the impact proof
negative_control: transfer to an invalid account fails, so success is not a default no-op

mutations.why: the guard may only apply to the first step

detected_by: ownership change without owner initiated event

counter.mechanism: owner consent required, two party confirmation
counter.precondition: the consent step must be server enforced

title: Soft delete resurrection
target_state: the deleted flag and its dependents
principal: the deleted object's former owner, or a new user
preconditions: delete is a flag, not a row delete
read paths filter the flag
write paths do not
or uniqueness indexes exclude soft deleted rows
procedure: delete an object you own
attempt update, share, restore and duplicate against the same id
re-register the same unique key and observe whether the old object resurfaces
oracle: object reappears in a listing
update on the deleted id succeeds
unique key collision reveals the hidden row
negative_control: a truly absent id fails, proving the resurrection is specific to soft deleted rows
detected_by: write to a soft deleted row

counter.mechanism: enforce the deleted predicate in the data layer, not the query layer

title: Bulk endpoint skips per item authorisation
preconditions: a batch, import or sync endpoint exists
it authorises the request, not each element
procedure: build a batch containing one object you own and one you do not
submit
observe partial success semantics
read back both
oracle: response reports per item status
the foreign item is modified and readable by its owner
negative_control: single object submission of the foreign id fails, isolating the finding to the batch path

counter.mechanism: authorise each element, report per element
counter.precondition: no early exit on first failure

title: Alternate representation reaches the same write with weaker checks
target_state: the same field, through a different parser
preconditions: the API accepts more than one content type or version
validation lives in one representation and not the other
procedure: identify the canonical JSON write
replay the same semantic operation as form encoded, XML, multipart, or a v1 path
compare validation and authorisation outcomes
oracle: the weaker representation persists a value the strict one rejects
negative_control: the strict representation rejects the same payload, proving the difference is the parser path
detected_by: non canonical content type on a write

counter.mechanism: one parser per resource, reject alternates

title: Write through an operation that was never designed as a write
preconditions: a read or compute endpoint mutates state as a side effect
the side effect is user influenceable
procedure: identify endpoints with side effects: view counters, exports, previews, previews of uploads, report generators
influence inputs so the side effect writes attacker chosen data
verify persistence across sessions
oracle: the derived value changes and persists
a fresh session sees it
negative_control: the same endpoint with benign input produces a different, expected derived value

counter.mechanism: no state change on safe methods

title: Authorisation evaluated on a stale copy of the object
principal: a user whose access was just revoked
preconditions: authorisation reads a cached or denormalised copy
the copy is refreshed lazily
revocation is not pushed
procedure: grant access, then revoke it
immediately attempt the write repeatedly
measure the window where the write still succeeds
oracle: write succeeds after revocation, and the audit log timestamp proves ordering
negative_control: the same write after the cache TTL fails, bounding the window
detected_by: access decision timestamp versus revocation timestamp

counter.mechanism: authorise against the authoritative store, or push invalidation synchronously

authorization: written scope, an account you can revoke
